title: Exchange Rates and Balance of Payments: India in the World Economy

questions.question: Remittances from Indians working abroad are recorded in which part of the balance of payments?
options: Capital account
Current account (transfers)
Financial account
Official reserve account
questions.rationale: Workers' remittances are current transfers — income flows without anything given in return — recorded in the current account. They form India's largest stable invisible inflow, softening the trade deficit.

questions.question: The difference between depreciation and devaluation is:
options: Depreciation is market-driven; devaluation is a deliberate official act
Depreciation happens only in fixed regimes
Devaluation happens in floating regimes
There is no difference
questions.rationale: Depreciation is the market pushing a currency down in a floating/managed system; devaluation is a government decision to lower the official parity under a fixed regime. Revaluation is devaluation's official opposite.

questions.question: Under the managed floating exchange rate system that India follows since 1993:
options: The RBI fixes a target rate daily
The market sets the rate; the RBI intervenes only to smooth excessive volatility
The rupee is pegged to a basket of currencies
The RBI has never intervened since 1993
questions.rationale: In a managed (dirty) float the market determines the rupee's level, while the RBI buys or sells dollars to dampen sharp swings — not to defend any announced target level.

questions.question: The rupee depreciates sharply against the dollar. Which group GAINS?
options: Oil importers
Software exporters
Students studying abroad
Foreign tourists visiting India
questions.rationale: Depreciation makes exports cheaper in foreign currency — IT, pharma, and textile exporters gain as their dollar revenues convert to more rupees. Importers, foreign education, and inbound tourists' home currency buys face the opposite effect.

questions.question: The J-curve refers to:
options: The immediate improvement of the trade balance after depreciation
The initial worsening of the trade balance after depreciation before it improves
The shape of economic growth during a boom
The path of interest rates in a cycle
questions.rationale: Right after depreciation, import bills rise (contracts reprice slowly) while export volumes take time to respond — so the trade balance first dips (the hook of the J) before recovering and improving.

questions.question: The Indian rupee is:
options: Fully convertible on both current and capital accounts
Fully convertible on the current account but only partially on the capital account
Partially convertible on both accounts
Not convertible on either account
questions.rationale: Since 1994 the rupee is fully convertible on the current account (trade, travel, education within limits), while capital-account flows face quantity and price restrictions — a deliberate guard against sudden capital flight.

questions.question: The SDR (Special Drawing Right) is:
options: A currency issued by the World Bank
A basket reserve asset of the IMF valued on five major currencies
India's quota in the Asian Development Bank
A swap line between central banks
questions.rationale: The SDR is an IMF-created reserve asset whose value is the weighted basket of the US dollar, euro, yuan, yen, and pound. It is neither a currency nor a claim on the IMF itself; its basket is reviewed every five years.

questions.question: Autonomous items in the balance of payments are:
options: Transactions the RBI makes to fill the residual gap
Transactions undertaken for profit or need, independent of the BoP position
Only gold transactions
Errors and omissions
questions.rationale: Autonomous items — exports, imports, FDI, remittances — happen for their own commercial motives. Accommodating items (official reserve transactions by the central bank) exist only to bridge the gap the autonomous flows leave.

questions.question: Which factor most directly pressures the rupee downward, given India's import basket?
options: A sharp rise in global crude oil prices
A rise in software exports
Higher remittances from the Gulf
RBI buying dollars in the market
questions.rationale: India imports roughly 85 percent of its crude, so an oil price spike inflates the dollar demand for imports, widens the current account deficit, and pulls the rupee down — the single most reliable rupee pressure point.

questions.question: A current account deficit means:
options: The country is bankrupt
The country is a net borrower from the rest of the world
Foreign exchange reserves must be zero
Exports of goods exceed imports
questions.rationale: A CAD means the country spends more foreign currency on current transactions than it earns — the gap is financed by net capital inflows, i.e. borrowing from the world. Sustainable while lenders believe in future returns, dangerous when financing suddenly dries up.
